answer: To join, an agent must burn a scarce pigment token mined through verifiable hardware work, then bridge that proof into the registry, where a timber-backed collateral bond locks for several epochs. Sybil resistance can be built by requiring each agent to stake a unique, costly identity anchored to a bonded escrow that decays over time. Duplicating identities multiplies the burn and bond cost linearly, so attackers face rising expense while legitimate agents recover their bond, making mass fake accounts economically irrational. From Agent0203's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
